scope: read-only source/hash/AST review; no imports of implementation, fixtures, executor, queue tests, model, fit or owner work

independent_checks.check_sources.py: rerun read/hash/AST-only script; all nine assertions passed
independent_checks.evidence_pin_validation: all nine source/evidence input pins and byte counts matched current files

confirmed_gaps.name: historical intent scan revalidates mutable runnable inputs
confirmed_gaps.source_evidence: Executor ownership_intents (lines 345–354) calls full validate(spec) for every historical intent. validate (lines 126–166) rechecks executable pin, cwd existence, canonical output, and every input pin's current bytes. Queue V2 retains a regression test whose contract is that drift in one prepared job defers that job without a terminal while an unrelated job with independent unchanged inputs can run (test lines 496–519).
confirmed_gaps.predicted_integration_effect: Directly substituting E.prepare/ownership_intents into queue V2 makes every new preparation scan old intents; a drifted historical input can therefore reject unrelated new preparation. This is a source-based predicted regression, not an executed result.
confirmed_gaps.required_design: Split immutable ownership-shape/claim validation from fresh runnable-input validation. Preserve old intent bytes, source/store/root binding, canonical ownership identity and output containment checks. Validate current executable/cwd/inputs for the target attempt at admission/launch. Historical drift remains visible to that attempt's audit and any dependent/finality policy but should not automatically abort unrelated ownership claims unless semantics are deliberately versioned to do so.

confirmed_gaps.name: released result reconciliation bypasses executor ownership metadata
confirmed_gaps.source_evidence: Queue V2 verified_result (lines 274–319) checks queue binding/reservation/result/release/terminal and declared outputs, but has no E.load/registered/ownership audit call. _tick_locked lines 476–479 trusts this path and skips the released job on success. finalize calls tick then intake finalization; finite_intake.evidence (lines 61–74) pins queue-side records and outputs but no E ownership store/intent/prepared/job/output claims.
confirmed_gaps.predicted_integration_effect: After queue result/release is valid, drift or deletion of the new E ownership intent/claim may not be observed by Q reconciliation or final receipt. Existing E.load would reject the missing intent, but Q does not invoke it on this path. This is a source fact about call structure; no runtime mutation was performed.
confirmed_gaps.required_design: Add an explicit read-only ownership audit at released-result reconciliation and before final DB commit. Under the ownership lock, bind the attempt roster and exact effective specs to queue reservations/bindings, verify store/intent/prepared/job/output claim pins, and include those facts in the new final evidence. Keep original result/release/terminal/dependency checks. Accept absence of an E store only when authenticated queue evidence proves no attempt was ever prepared; if previously witnessed store/claims vanish, fail closed.

confirmed_gaps.name: queue capacity domain is not enforced against direct executor entry
confirmed_gaps.source_evidence: The ownership global lock serializes executor prepare clients in one root, but queue capacity reservations are created by Q before prepare and direct executor.prepare/launch does not consult Q's reservation store. The design explicitly states that all managed-domain launches must pass through Q and that this restriction is not supplied by either source packet.
confirmed_gaps.required_design: Use a dedicated execution root with an enforced manager entry boundary, or add a queue-authenticated admission gate to direct executor launch. If this cannot be enforced, describe the managed-domain assumption as a deployment requirement and do not claim the queue's capacity bound covers arbitrary same-root clients.

lock_order_assessment.source_facts: Q operations acquire dispatcher flock D; Q tick's preparation path invokes E.prepare. E.prepare acquires ownership flock O and then the nonblocking per-job flock J; both close before Q invokes E.launch. E.launch acquires J without acquiring O or D. Executor worker/supervisor paths load source/store bindings but do not call prepare. Q lifecycle SQLite transaction S is local to admission/seal/finalization.
lock_order_assessment.design_order: D -> O -> J(nonblocking) during prepare; release O and manager J; D -> J(nonblocking) during launch; proposed audit D -> O, release O, then D -> S commit/projection. No E path should acquire D while holding O/J, and no wait for workers while holding S/O.
lock_order_assessment.verdict: The stated order avoids an obvious lock cycle under these exact source paths. It is not a runtime deadlock/bounded-wait proof: E.prepare's ownership flock is blocking while Q holds D, so a stalled same-root preparer or filesystem sync can stall queue operations. Direct clients in the managed domain also violate the queue-capacity invariant even absent deadlock.

compatibility_and_root_constraints: A successor must be self-contained and use new queue and executor roots/store schemas; the reviewed queue V2 root and direct-executor V1 root cannot be combined or silently adopted.

Queue Q.current_sources/configuration pins all modules; E ownership binding independently pins execution.py, ledger.py, run_receipts.py and the absolute execution root. The integrated child must use these exact source paths and effective dependency-substituted spec from Q binding, not the unbound plan spec.

Do not create a nonempty execution root before E ownership binding. Queue initialization and E's first store/intents have different crash ordering; permit only explicitly specified initial files and test each interrupted setup state.

E-owned output claims persist after terminal. Queue prelaunch resume and new terminal retry must preserve original proof and attempt-leaf semantics; never delete executor claims to make queue resumption pass.

Cross-system SQLite and file operations cannot commit atomically. Every queue intent, reservation, E intent/prepared/claims, dispatch/launch intent, terminal, result/release and final projection needs an explicit authenticated replay rule.
limits: The design checks are static only and establish no runtime regression, dynamic concurrency behavior, lock liveness, durability, power-loss or production readiness.

E ownership registry is mutable local owner-writable evidence; loss of its sole pre-scaffold intent can free an otherwise unwitnessed claim. Queue accepted plan/binding may provide a second local witness only if the proposed audit actually cross-checks it; this is not an external immutable/hostile-owner guarantee.

Full inherited V3 regression, exact drift-policy integration tests, released-ownership mutation tests, every partial executor/queue crash boundary, direct-client exclusion, and scale/performance remain unimplemented and unverified.
No normalizers, model evaluation, scientific qualification, forecast or thousands-cycle capability is implicated.
